result.topic_en: Euler gives other reductions of the form 40aa+13bb for testing primality. Suitable substitutions remove the factor 40 (or 13), so that a sequence of numbers with constant second differences is subtracted successively from a square.
result.transcription:
— 30 —

ubi differentiae iterum manifesto augmento constanti 260 crescunt, quas igitur loco S continuo ab ipso quadrato $aa$ subtrahi oportet.

Alia Evolutio
numerorum formae $40aa+13bb$.

§. 49. Cum habeatur aequatio: $40aa-13(yy-bb)=40xx$, tollamus primo tantum factorem parem 8, et quia $b$ denotat numerum imparem, evidens est, dummodo pro $y$ etiam sumatur numerus impar, formulam $yy-bb$ fore divisibilem per 8. Ponatur igitur in genere $y=2z\pm b$, et facta divisione per 8 habebimus hanc aequationem:
$5aa-\frac{13}{2}(zz\pm bz)=5xx$; ubi evidens est, membrum medium semper esse integrum. Nunc igitur loco $z$ talem numerum assumi oportet, ut vel $z$, vel $z\pm b$ factorem habeat 5: perinde autem est uter horum factorum per 5 divisibilis reddatur, propterea quod inter se sunt permutabiles, mutato scilicet signo ipsius $b$. Ponatur igitur $z=5s$ et facta divisione per 5 aequatio, cui satisfieri oportet, erit:
$aa-\frac{13}{2}(5ss\pm bs)=xx$.

§. 50. Hic igitur a quadrato $aa$ subtrahi debent numeri in forma $\frac{13}{2}(5ss\pm bs)$ contenti, quae si vocetur $=$ S, valores ipsius S erunt, uti in sequenti tabula cum suis differentiis exhibentur.

$s$ | S | Diff.
$0$ | $0$ | $\frac{13}{2}(5\pm b)$
$\pm 1$ | $\frac{13}{2}(5\pm b)$ | $\frac{13}{2}(15\pm b)$
$\pm 2$ | $\frac{13}{2}(20\pm 2b)$ | $\frac{13}{2}(45\mp b)$ [?]
$\pm 3$ | $\frac{13}{2}(45\pm 3b)$ | $\frac{13}{2}(35\pm b)$
$\pm 4$ | $\frac{13}{2}(80+4b)$ |
etc. | etc. | etc.

ubi

— 31 —

ubi differentiae, quas a quadrato $aa$ continuo subtrahi oportet, augmento constanti $\frac{13}{2}\cdot 10=65$ crescunt.

§. 51. Quin etiam unica substitutione totus numerus 40 statim tolli potest, ponendo $y=10s\pm b$; tum enim ob $yy-bb=100ss\pm 20bs$, dividendo per 40 statim pervenitur ad hanc aequationem: $aa-\frac{13}{2}(5ss\pm bs)=xx$, uti modo invenimus. Hoc igitur artificio semper uti licebit, quoties littera $\alpha$ valorem habeat parem, atque adeo cum potestate binarii simul unum factorem primum tollere licebit. Veluti si $\alpha=2^{\lambda}\cdot fg$, ita ut formula $yy-bb$ per hunc valorem divisibilis reddi debeat, statim poni poterit:
$y=2^{\lambda-1}fz\pm b$; tum enim erit:
$yy-bb=2^{2\lambda-2}ffzz\pm 2^{\lambda}bfz$, quae forma per $2^{\lambda}f$ divisa abit in hanc:
$2^{\lambda-2}fzz\pm bz$, quod igitur cum fuerit praefixum, reliqui factores per praecepta generalia, alibi tradita, facile e medio tolli poterunt. Est adhuc alia, eaque simplicissima evolutio formulae $N=40aa+13bb$.

§. 52. Cum posito $N=40xx+13yy$ aequatio prima fundamentalis hoc modo repraesentetur: $13bb-40(xx-aa)=13yy$, observasse juvabit, eam unica operatione resolvi posse, ponendo $x=13s+a$. Facta enim substitutione et divisione per 13 pervenietur ad hanc aequationem simplicissimam: $bb-40(13ss+2as)=yy$. Hic igitur a quadrato $bb$ successive subtrahi debent valores formulae: $40(13ss\pm 2as)$, qui illa (posita hac formula br. gr. $=$ S) ordine cum suis differentiis disponuntur:

items.quote: et quia $b$ denotat numerum imparem, evidens est, dummodo pro $y$ etiam sumatur numerus impar, formulam $yy-bb$ fore divisibilem per 8.
items.english: Since b denotes an odd number, it is evident that, provided an odd number is also taken for y, the expression yy − bb will be divisible by 8.

items.quote: ubi evidens est, membrum medium semper esse integrum.
items.english: Here it is evident that the middle term is always an integer.

items.quote: Quin etiam unica substitutione totus numerus 40 statim tolli potest, ponendo $y=10s\pm b$
items.english: Indeed, the whole number 40 can be removed at once by a single substitution, setting y = 10s ± b.

items.quote: Hoc igitur artificio semper uti licebit, quoties littera $\alpha$ valorem habeat parem, atque adeo cum potestate binarii simul unum factorem primum tollere licebit.
items.english: This device can therefore always be used whenever the letter α has an even value; and together with the power of two, one prime factor can be removed at the same time.

items.quote: reliqui factores per praecepta generalia, alibi tradita, facile e medio tolli poterunt.
items.english: The remaining factors can easily be eliminated by the general rules given elsewhere.

items.quote: observasse juvabit, eam unica operatione resolvi posse, ponendo $x=13s+a$.
items.english: It will help to observe that it can be resolved by a single operation, setting x = 13s + a.
